map.An area, surface area & volume adventure: A story about area, surface area & volume, in five chapters. It has six reader gates. Solve the math to move the story.
map.Pattern distortion detected in a set of: Bent patterns found in some blueprints. Reader: bring a pencil.
map.Previously: a night-market stall yelled: Last time: a night-market stall yelled "50% OFF EVERYTHING" and lied with every percent. The crew worked backwards from the parts and exposed the scam. The pier fund hit 100%. The whole city watched.
map.The city picked OUR design. Skate ramp,: The city picked OUR design! Skate ramp, stage, garden beds, storage shed. Brightside comes back.
map.We beat one other bidder: Hargrove & Son: We beat one other bidder: Hargrove & Sons. Their bid was strangely cheap.
map.Warning: Hargrove's blueprints hum with: Warning: Hargrove's blueprints hum and look wrong. Their measurements are... bent.
map.It's a parallelogram. Slice a triangle o: It's a parallelogram. Cut a triangle off one end. Slide it to the other end. Now it IS a rectangle. Whole, not half.
map.Vocabulary upload. The base is the side: Vocabulary upload. The base is the side you stand on. The height is the straight-up distance to the opposite side. Never use the slanted edge. Area = base × height.
map.To decompose a shape means to cut it int: To decompose a shape means to cut it into pieces you already know. Mina's slice-and-slide turns a parallelogram into a rectangle. It has the same base, height, and area.
map.The blueprint shows the stage floor: a p: The blueprint shows the stage floor. It is a parallelogram with base 12 ft and height 7 ft. Hargrove says "charge for half." Find the TRUE area in square feet.
map.Conceptual: a parallelogram is a pushed-: Conceptual: a parallelogram is a rectangle that was pushed over. Cut a triangle off one end and slide it to the other. Nothing gets cut in half.
map.Procedural: multiply base × height. Do N: Procedural: multiply base × height. Do NOT divide by 2. That is only for triangles.
map.Shade sail over the stage. It's literall: Shade sail over the stage. It's a parallelogram folded in half. Triangle class, level one.
map.So same move as the floor… then take hal: So we do the same as the floor... then take half. The fabric bill depends on it.
map.Confirmed. Two copies of any triangle sn: Yes. Two copies of any triangle fit together into a parallelogram. So a triangle's area = base × height ÷ 2.
map.Noah tested it on scrap fabric: a little: Noah tested it on scrap fabric. A little triangle with base 6 and height 8 had an area of 24 square units. That is half of 48. The ÷ 2 is a must.
map.Order the sail fabric, reader. Too littl: Order the sail fabric, reader. Too little = sunburn. Too much = no money.
map.Conceptual: two copies of this sail woul: Conceptual: two copies of this sail would fit together into a parallelogram. You need only ONE sail.
map.Procedural: multiply base × height, then: Procedural: multiply base × height. Then take half of that.
map.East corner of the lot. The beds taper s: East corner of the lot. The beds get narrow so wheelbarrows can pass.
map.Trapezoid bed: two parallel sides — a sh: Trapezoid bed: it has two parallel sides, a short base and a long base. The height runs straight between them.
map.Hargrove's flyer says beds like ours nee: Hargrove's flyer says beds like ours need "double" the liner. VEX glitches just from reading it.
map.Trapezoid trick: it's an in-between rect: Trapezoid trick: it works like a rectangle in between. Average the two bases. Add them, then divide by 2. Then multiply by the height.
map.Mina proved it on the whiteboard with ba: Mina showed it on the whiteboard with bases 6 and 10 and height 4. The average base is 8, so the area is 32. Decompose it into a rectangle plus two triangles. You get the same answer.
Liner fabric is cut to the square foot. Measure the bed exactly, reader.
map.Conceptual: a trapezoid acts like an in-: Conceptual: a trapezoid acts like a rectangle in the middle. Its true width is the AVERAGE of the short base and the long base.
map.Procedural: add the two bases, divide by: Procedural: add the two bases. Divide by 2. Then multiply by the height.
map.Planter boxes for the herbs. Volume tell: Planter boxes for the herbs. Volume tells us how much soil fits inside. We measure it in cubic feet, like stacking blocks.
map.Except our edges aren't whole numbers. T: But our edges are not whole numbers. The blocks come in halves now.
map.Formula holds anyway: volume = length ×: The formula still works: volume = length × width × height. It works with fraction edges too. Noah's test box, 3 × 1.5 × 2, holds exactly 9 cubic feet.
map.Half-blocks still count. A layer of half: Half-blocks still count. A layer of half-foot cubes is just a thinner layer. Multiply it in like any other number.
map.The soil truck is idling, reader. How ma: The soil truck is waiting, reader. How many cubic feet does one planter hold?
map.One planter box measures 4 ft × 2.5 ft ×: One planter box measures 4 ft × 2.5 ft × 1.5 ft. How many cubic feet of soil fill it to the top?
map.Conceptual: volume is length × width × h: Conceptual: volume is length × width × height. Fraction edges multiply just like whole numbers. A half-foot layer is simply a thinner layer.
map.Procedural: multiply 4 × 2.5 first, then: Procedural: first multiply 4 × 2.5. Then multiply that answer by 1.5.
map.That flat shape is a net. Fold it back u: That flat shape is a net. Fold it back up and you get the box. Add the areas of all six faces and you get the surface area. That is the box's whole skin.
map.Shortcut: a box has three different face: Shortcut: a box has three different faces, and each shows up twice. Find the three, add them, and double the total.
The storage crate is 4 ft × 3 ft × 2 ft. Step 1: tap the net that really folds into this crate. Step 2: enter its surface area, the plywood for ALL the faces.
map.Conceptual: a closed box needs 6 faces,: Conceptual: a closed box needs 6 faces. Opposite faces are twins, the same size, in pairs. A true net has exactly the right 6.
map.Procedural: the three different faces ar: Procedural: the three different faces are 4×3, 4×2, and 3×2. Find each area. Add the three. Then double the total.
map.City Hall, 6 PM. The council will fund w: City Hall, 6 PM. The council will fund the bid that "adds up." Hargrove smiles like a crocodile.
map.Distortion source located: that bid. The: Source of the bent numbers: that bid. The shed is 5 × 4 × 3 feet. The garden bed is 6 × 2 × 1.5. Check everything.
map.Reader — paint covers faces, soil fills: Reader, paint covers faces and soil fills space. Work out our honest numbers. Then we call the vote.
map.Boss Gate: surface area for the paint, v: Boss Gate: surface area for the paint, volume for the soil, and one last choice. Everything from this volume, all at once.
map.The council votes tonight. Hargrove's bi: The council votes tonight. Hargrove's bid says 54 sq ft of paint for the shed and 12 cu ft of soil for each bed. The real shed is 5 × 4 × 3 ft. The real bed is 6 × 2 × 1.5 ft. Three locks:
map.Conceptual: paint covers FACES — that's: Conceptual: paint covers FACES. That is surface area, all six faces. Soil fills SPACE. That is volume. These are two different questions about the same boxes.
map.Built from an honest blueprint: 84 for t: Built from an honest blueprint: 84 for the stage, 30 for the sail, 50 for each bed. And every face of that shed gets paint.
map.The council audited Hargrove's \"54.\" T: The council checked Hargrove's "54." Two faces were missing. He is banned from city bids for a year.
map.New distortion. A vault door under Vexha: A new bent pattern. A vault door under Vexhall, covered in symbols. To be continued...
map.Builder, artist, this volume's crew lead: Builder and artist, and this volume's crew lead. Drew the winning blueprint. Sliced a parallelogram into a rectangle while a real contractor watched.
map.Crew captain. Kept the build on schedule: Crew captain. Kept the build on time and wrote every base and every height in the notebook.
map.Evidence officer. Audited Hargrove's bid: Evidence officer. Checked Hargrove's bid down to the last missing face. "Trust us" is not a unit.
map.Pattern hunter. Treats volume like block: Pattern hunter. Thinks of volume like stacking blocks in a video game. And, annoyingly, is right.
map.Fragment of Ada Vex's Pattern Engine. Se: A piece of Ada Vex's Pattern Engine. Senses bent patterns but cannot compute. That's your job.
map.Base & height.The base is a side; the he: Base & height.The base is a side. The height is the straight-up distance to the opposite side, never the slant.
map.Volume.Space inside, in cubic units: len: Volume.The space inside, in cubic units: length × width × height. Fractions work too. Planter: 4 × 2.5 × 1.5 = 15 cu ft.
map.Net & surface area.Unfold the box into a: Net & surface area.Unfold the box into a net. Add all six faces. Crate: 2(12 + 8 + 6) = 52 sq ft of skin.
map.completed Volume 5: Blueprint for Bright: completed Volume 5: Blueprint for Brightside and showed skill with areas of parallelograms, triangles, and trapezoids, volume with fractional edges, nets, and surface area.
map.Check by decomposing: slice the slanted: Check by decomposing: cut off the slanted end and slide it across. You get a 9 × 4 rectangle. Same 36.
map.12 × 7 = 84 sq ft — the whole floor, no: 12 × 7 = 84 sq ft. The whole floor, no Hargrove cut. Stage: funded!
map.You charged for half the stage! The ÷ 2: You charged for half the stage! The ÷ 2 is only for triangles. Slice-and-slide keeps a parallelogram whole.
map.Use base × height — the dashed 7 ft, not: Use base × height. Use the dashed 7 ft, not a slanted edge.
map.That buys a whole parallelogram of fabri: That buys a whole parallelogram of fabric. The sail is HALF of it. One more step.
map.Base × height first… then remember what: Do base × height first. Then remember what a triangle is half of.
map.That's Hargrove's 'double' — you added t: That is Hargrove's 'double.' You added the bases but skipped the ÷ 2. Average them first.
map.Average the two bases (add, then halve),: Average the two bases: add, then halve. THEN multiply by the height.
map.Someone rounded the edges down to whole: Someone rounded the edges down to whole numbers. The 2.5 and the 1.5 count, halves and all.
map.Good start — that's 4 × 2.5. Now multipl: Good start. That's 4 × 2.5. Now multiply by the height, 1.5.
map.Length × width × height. Multiply all th: Length × width × height. Multiply all three edges. Fractions count too.
map.Step 1 first — tap the net that folds in: Do Step 1 first. Tap the net that folds into the crate.
map.Count the faces on that net. A closed cr: Count the faces on that net. A closed crate needs 6. Tools would fall out of this one.
map.Check the end flaps: square 3 × 3 ends c: Check the end flaps. Square 3 × 3 ends can't close a crate that is 3 ft by 2 ft deep.
map.Net A folds tight, and 2(12 + 8 + 6) = 5: Net A folds up tight, and 2(12 + 8 + 6) = 52 sq ft of plywood. Crates: done!
map.You found the three different faces — bu: You found the three different faces. But every face has a twin. Double it.
map.That's how much the crate HOLDS (volume): That is how much the crate HOLDS (volume). Surface area is the skin, not what's inside.
map.Add the three different face areas, then: Add the three different face areas. Then double the total for the twin faces.
map.Lock 1 holds. That's Hargrove's number —: Lock 1 holds. That's Hargrove's number. He skipped two faces. 2 × (lw + lh + wh) counts all six.
map.Lock 1 holds. Three face pairs: 5·4, 5·3: Lock 1 holds. Three face pairs: 5·4, 5·3, 4·3. Add them, then double.
map.Lock 2 holds. Someone flattened the 1.5: Lock 2 holds. Someone changed the 1.5 into a 1. The half-foot of depth is real soil.
map.ALL LOCKS OPEN. 94 honest square feet, 1: ALL LOCKS OPEN. 94 honest square feet, 18 true cubic feet. The council tears up Hargrove's bid. Brightside gets built RIGHT!
